references.text: Describes the same menorah (lampstand) and its branches, which verse 33 continues to detail with bowls shaped like almond blossoms.
Continues the description of the menorah's decorations with almond-shaped bowls, buds, and flowers on the main stem of the lampstand.
Parallel text describing the actual construction of the menorah's branches, each featuring three almond-shaped bowls, a bud, and a flower.
The complete account of Bezalel's execution of the menorah in accordance with the instructions given in chapter 25.
Refers to the menorah's construction with floral work, confirming the execution of the design described in Exodus 25:33.
Aaron's staff that budded with almond blossoms connects to the almond motif (meshukadim) used in the menorah's decoration.
The prophet Jeremiah sees an almond branch (shaked), which shares a root with the word for almond-shaped bowls (meshukadim) in the menorah's design.
Zechariah's vision of a golden lampstand (menorah) with seven lamps, drawing from the tabernacle's lampstand described in Exodus.
Complementary description of the same object; together the verses provide a holistic understanding of the lampstand's complex design.
A complementary detail that, along with the source verse, completes the description of the lampstand's botanical symbolism.
Structural prerequisite for the decoration; together they provide a complete picture of the lampstand's architecture.
Historical fulfillment and expansion of the motif; showing continuity in God's house from the wilderness to Solomon's temple.
